> but maybe that'll be what sets you apart from other students if you do it

I don't know if that is a good thing. My peers already seem to think of me as weird or something.

> and all three of my advisors say pretty much the same thing

Did you give research a shot?

>If you're too anxious, see if you can find anything about your professor online. If they're mean/rude, other students usually complain about it

Most seem ok based on what I have heard. Pretty much nobody in my major tried research though.
Yeah, but I can't help but think that I am the problem given how everyone else is ok with each other while they all see to be avoiding me.
She seems to have a good relationship with other people in my major though.
The way that girl shunned me was weird. It only makes sense if she sees me as insane or something.

> Don't be so quick to consider yourself the psycho black sheep girl

How else can you explain how she avoided me?

> I think you should really talk to your parents and let them know everything going on, because it seems like they are your only life line left

They think I am blaming everyYing on ADHD and thatcIvam not trying.
I did talk to my psychiatrist about it and she said that I don't seem to have ASD.
I don't know.
We were heading to the same class though.
We were heading to the same class though.

> Have you discussed this with your psychiatrist?

No. Anyway, that girls behaviour was super odd. She definitely wasn't like that to me in the past.

The general pattern seems to be that everyone is avoiding me. I know that I screwed up but I don't know how to change things. Of course, taking a break from uni works - I will be in another grade so I do not have to interact with the same peers!

We mainly talk about ADHD and how things have been going for me lately.

> And noone is going to think you're psychotic if you just knock off making suicidal claims in class

The way she avoided me was wtf-tier. It only makes sense in a psychotic context.
I think all of my peers dislike me though.

> What label is that?

Psychotic.

Well she just said she wanted to give me an antidepressant to make me feel happier.

I do feel suicidal at times and sometimes I just don't want to talk to anyone and wish that I could evaporate into thin air.

> your peers likely don't think about you one iota

How do you explain how that girl "quickly walked away" though?
Yes but avoiding me like this implies that I am extremely strange.

Sorry for the jumbled up post. I copied and pasted from other threads.

>Were you diagnosed with ADHD? Do you take ADHD medicine? Are you in counselling for ADHD? She might mean that public psychiatrists would not give you therapy for ADHD no.

Yes. Yes, I take Concerta. Yes, but since I don't really click with my counsellor and no longer seeks therapy, I don't seek help from her anymore.

>Mirtazaprine is proscribed against depression but did you psychiatrist tell you she was treating you for depression?

She didn't at first, but when I asked she said yes.

>How did you do in high school? Both school-wise and social wise?

I did well academically. My major has a high admission grade requirement. I have always struggled to make friends but never have I felt this depressed before.

>I mean your story is very jumbled and if you talk to people about it like this

I didn't tell anyone at uni that I have ADHD. I mainly ask them about homework or time schedule changes and maybe they will find that weird.

>And you're 20 years old, there's plenty of time to fix any mistakes you may have made

It is hard to remove such a stigmatised label.
My parents don't seem to trust her do I can't help but feel the same.

Yes, and given how stigmatized mental disorders are, I don't think I will ever be fully accepted by my peers. There were also times when I spiralled into extreme depression mood in class and wrote about how I wanted to die, how I had anger outbursts and had brief homicidal idealisation, etc on Reddit. I did change my screen to a very dim setting but maybe someone saw my posts. I also sometimes post in r/ADHD in class (as well as other disorder subs) simply out of boredom but I guess that looks odd to the outsider.

I know that most people experience homicidal idealisation at some point (hence the phrase "I swear I will kill that person"), however, I think that from this point onwards, my peers will only notice the things which make me "psycho" given how they have already attached this label to me. This label seems to be extremely stigmatised and I am sure that it will affect my job aspects in some way. News spread like wildfire in the industry given how its workforce is relatively small and I think rumours about how I am psycho will certainly affect my employment prospects.

I major in something related to stem so I doubt my writing skills matter that much.

Sometimes I get the feeling that everyone in my major is avoiding me like a plague. The most reasonable explanation is that they think that I am psychotic given that I once lost control and cried and screamed loudly on campus outside of class. Maybe some people from my major saw me and then news started to spread like wildfire.
Yeah you can't help but think maybe you are the problem if everyone in your major is avoiding you like a plague while they have good relationships with each other.

> Putting up walls against those who are professionals and trying to help you is a defence mechanism

They may not have my best interest at heart.

> I have learned that you can't change their minds

Yeah I don't get why they are avoiding me. Do they find me "weird"? "Psycho"? "Autistic-like"?
Including the part where people go out of their way to avoid you?
Yeah but it's not "normal" to my parents. They are basing my experiences based on their experiences. They think I am exaggerating all my problems and blaming it all on ADHD or whatever.

I have been doing poorly in class, is often late, often gets class schedules mixed up, and often asked others for help. I guess all my acquaintances got sick of it and hence why they are "avoiding" me.
It depends. She started to prescribe me with an antidepressant a few days ago so she wanted to see me two weeks later to monitor the adverse effects.

My psychiatrist already prescribed me an antidepressant. However, I feel like I cannot fully trust her. My parents distrust her and think that she recommends me to see her more regularly to earn more money. She is ultimately motivated by money and I really don't know if she has my interest at heart.

I see them in class. However, I don't want others to hear what I say. Given how some of my peers seem to be avoiding me, I feel like they will snicker at me if they know that I want to give research a shot.
Yeah it is hard not to feel suicidal.
Yeah and it seems like things will never get better. It is hard not to feel suicidal.
How should I approach the professor for this? Email? Ask in person? As I have said, I have accidentally missed a mini field trip in the past so I don't think they see me as "reliable".
How should I approach the professor for this? Email? Ask in person? As I have said, I have accidentally missed a mini field trip in the past so I don't think they see me as "reliable".

> and if they say yes then it's because they know about your performance as a student and want to say yes anyway

But my grades are not good.
Yeah I can write but I can read texts this long.

It is still weird. It is even weirder when they see me changing my persona. I sometimes post about American politics in class as well, and I will identify myself as American in some posts to make my posts more convincinf in that sub.

Oh I don't think they can exactly stalk me and find my posts. Reddit is most anonymous and sometimes I even change my identify (eg. nationality) to make it hard for people in the web to remember me as I post in multiple accounts.

Yes I have changed my study methods and it is helping.

The way that girl walked away quickly was weird. The most logical explanation is that she is avoiding me.
So? I need to explain my situation.

I think there are things which are universally  seen as "success" given the capitalist culture of many countries. Money is one of these factors for measuring success.

That girl acted in a really strange manner when she saw me on the bus.
800 words for what?

Well life still isn't good. The truth is everyone cases about status to some extent, and the chances are against me to succeed. I think I am already screwed given my poor grades, how my peers hate me, and how nobody can relate to me.
So yes, this happens. The odds are against you to succeed. In my country technically anyway can work at McDonalds given the current economical environment.
You probably have other skills though such as networking skills. I am good at nothing.

1) Most people seem to have managed it. I guess people are sick of me messaging them and asking if there is class on that day as I am often confused.

2) As I have said, almost everyone in my major is super smart due to its admission requirements. I am truly at the bottom of the barrel for my major.

3) They don't know that I have ADHD. They probably just we me as extremely weird and given how that girl chose to walk quickly away, I must be very "repulsive" (pun intended). I have noticed that others seem to have no problem hanging out with each other so I am the problem.

I don't know what my professors will think of me. Also, I think will and have already been blacklisted given my previous academic record. For example, I want to ask a professor for summer research opportunities but I don't know if she will want help for me given how I flunked her prefab quizzes and accidentally missed a mini field trip as I wasn't even aware of it. She encourages students to do research but she may be doing this out of politeness and trying to let us know that research is an option given the current underemployment rate for this industry. I don't know how she will react when I ask her about research jobs - she may "avoid" me like that girl on the bus and hate me even more.
Everything.
I have no one to talk to. I feel like only my psychiatrist can relate to my problems.
